first_end.mechanism: expiration of term: EO 12193 (sole operative sentence) 'I hereby extend the duration of that period to March 10,1981.' (the period in the first proviso to sec. 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act; held official FR text, 45 FR 9885). The extension it granted ran out on 1981-03-10. The next extension was made by a separate determination, EO 12295 (signed February 24, 1981, 46 FR 14113, held, read: 'upon the expiration of the period specified in the first proviso to Section 126a(2) of such Act and extended by Executive Order 12193 ... I hereby extend the duration of that period to March 10, 1982.'), which recites EO 12193 as the earlier extension but neither amends nor continues it. EO 12553 later revoked the spent order (1986-02-25)

Executive Order 12193 of February 12, 1980
Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  
the United States of America, including Section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy  
Act of 1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2155(a)(2)), and having determined that,  
upon the expiration of the period specified in the first proviso to Section  
126a(2) of such Act, failure to continue peaceful nuclear cooperation with the  
European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to the  
achievement of the United States non-proliferation objectives and would  
otherwise jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States,  
and having notified the Congress of this determination, I hereby extend the  
duration of that period to March 10,1981.
F e b r u a r y  12, 1980.
Editorial Note: The text of the President’s letters to the Speaker of the House and the President  
of the Senate, dated Feb. 7,1980, on exports of nuclear fuels, is printed in the Weekly Compilation  
of Presidential Documents (vol. 16, p. 286).
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Determination under sec. 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act that failing to continue nuclear cooperation with EURATOM would be seriously prejudicial, and extension of the sec. 126a(2) period to March 10, 1981. Ended with the whole order: first end EO 12193, 1981-03-10. The order's only operative content is an extension of a statutory period to a fixed date, March 10, 1981; that is a fixed date, not a report deadline. Later event attached: EO 12553 revocation (1986-02-25), which does not move the first end.

later_events.mechanism: formal revocation after the end: express revocation by EO 12553 ('it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:', followed by the table row 12193 'Providing for nuclear cooperation with EURATOM'); EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986); the extension had already run out on 1981-03-10, so this clears a spent order and does not move the first end

research_rationale: EO 12193 (signed 1980-02-12, 45 FR 9885), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence making a sec. 126a(2) determination and extending the period to March 10, 1981. The dossier's machine inventory (scopes #lead, #1980, #1, #2, #3, #4, #1980-dup2) starts mid-sentence at 'I hereby extend' and otherwise takes in the editorial note, a blank page and the neighbouring Rules and Regulations documents on PDF pages 10-11, which are not part of EO 12193; a corrected inventory of one span (enacting and determination words through 'March 10,1981.', offsets 731-1471) replaces it. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12193>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's only operative content is an extension of a statutory period to a fixed date, March 10, 1981; that is a fixed date, not a report deadline. Held orders naming 12193 are EO 12295, EO 12553 and later EURATOM extension orders (EO 12351, 12409, 12463, 12506, 12554, 12587, 12629, 12670, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840, 12903, 12955), each read in the relevant part: they recite EO 12193 in the list of orders that extended the period and then extend it again by their own determination; none amends, suspends or revives EO 12193. EO 12295 (signed 1981-02-24, before the 1981-03-10 expiry) extends the period from March 10, 1981 to March 10, 1982 by its own determination; it does not say it amends or supersedes EO 12193, so EO 12193's extension ran its full term and EO 12295's took over at its end. The dossier's machine 'supersede' chain records from EO 12629, 12706, 12791, 12840, 12903 and 12955 are misattributions: each of those orders supersedes only its immediate predecessor, not EO 12193, and all are after 1986. The dossier gaps 'target provision not located' for EO 12295, 12351, 12506, 12554 and 12753 are OFR 'See' cross-references (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv kind cross_reference), not events: their held texts contain no provision acting on EO 12193, only recitals, so they are closed as recitals, not left as material gaps. EO 12554 (1986-02-28) still recites EO 12193 three days after its revocation, which confirms the recital is history, not continuation. The EO 12593 hit is an index number and the EO 9920 hit is a file SHA-256 string. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is the 1981-03-10 expiry, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. Whether a recital in a later extension keeps an expired extension order alive is not asserted by any held source; the producer reads the recitals as history. Nothing relies on the pending report-deadline or transcription-as-copy rulings. First end: EO 12193, 1981-03-10. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 12193 in full: it made one determination and extended a statutory period to 1981-03-10; cooperation with EURATOM during that year was a completed matter, and every later year rests on its own extension order. It created no office, fund, property or private right. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlived 1981-03-10. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

a c t io n: Final rule; correction.
s u m m a r y: The final rulemaking 
published in the Federal Register on 
Thursday, December 13,1979 (44 FR
72089), on the Sugarcane Crop Insurance  
Regulations, Amendment No. 2, 
inadvertently omitted a county in 
Florida where such insurance is 
authorized to be offered. This notice is 
being published to correct that error. 
EFFECTIVE DATE: February 14,1980.  
a d d r e s s: Any suggestions or inquiries 
on this notice should be sent to James D. 
Deal, Manager, Federal Crop Insurance  
Corporation, U.S. Department of 
Agriculture, Washington, D.C. 20250.

Peter F. Cole, Secretary, Federal Crop  
Insurance Corporation, U.S. Department 
of Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250, 
telephone 202-447-3325.
The correction is as follow^:
In the “Appendix B” of 7 CFR Part 417,  
as appearing on page 72089 (44 FR  
72089), the list of counties under the 
subheading “Florida” is hereby 
corrected by inserting alphabetically the  
word “Hendry" after the word "Glades”  
and before the words “Palm Beach”.
Issued in Washington, D.C., on February 6, 
1980.
Peter F. Cole,
Secretary, Federal Crop Insurance 
Corporation.

7 CFR Part 418
W heat Crop Insurance R eg u la tio n s - 
Amendment No. 1; Corrections
AGENCY: Federal Crop Insurance  
Corporation.
ACTION: Final rule; corrections.
SUMMARY: The final rulemaking 
published in the Federal Register on  
Thursday, December 13,1979 (44 FR
72090) , on the Wheat Crop Insurance  
Regulations, Amendment No. 1, 
contained inadvertent omissions of  
county names and a typographical error.  
This notice is being published to correct  
those errors.
EFFECTIVE DATE: February 14,1980.
ADDRESS: Any suggestions or inquires 
on this notice should be sent to James D.  
Deal, Manager, Federal Crop Insurance  
Corporation, U.S. Department of  
Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:  
Peter F. Cole, Secretary, Federal Crop  
Insurance Corporation, U.S. Department  
of Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250,  
telephone 202-447-3325.
The corrections are as follows:
1. The list of counties where wheat  
crop insurance is offered, as appearing  
in the left column of page 72091 (44 FR
72091) , is corrected by inserting, after  
the listing for Alabama and before the  
listing for Arkansas, the following:
Arizona
Maricopa, Pinal, Yuma.
2. Under the subheading “Idaho” in  
the list of counties as appearing in the  
center column on page 72091 (44 FR  
72091), insert the word “Elmore”  
between the words “Cassia” and  
"Franklin”.
3. Under the subheading “Minnesota”  
in the list of counties as appearing in the  
left column on page 72092 (44 FR 72092),  
the correct spelling of “McCleod” is  
"McLeod”.
4. Under the subheading "South  
Dakota” in the list of counties as  
appearing in the right column on page 
72092 (44 FR 72092), insert the words  
“Charles Mix" between the words  
“Campbell” and “Clark”.
1980.
Peter F. Cole,
Secretary, Federal Crop Insurance 
Corporation.

7 CFR Part 428
Sunflower Crop Insurance  
Regulations—Amendment No. 1;  
Correction
AGENCY: Federal Crop Insurance  
Corporation.
ACTION: Final rule; correction.
SUMMARY: The final rulemaking 
published in the Federal Register on  
Thursday, December 20,1979 (44 FR  
75373-75374), on the Sunflower Crop  
Insurance Regulations, Amendment No.  
1, did not list two North Dakota  
Counties which were inadvertently  
omitted. This notice is being published 
to correct that error.
EFFECTIVE DATE: February 14,1980.
ADDRESS: Any suggestions or inquiries 
on this notice should be sent to James D.  
Deal, Manager, Federal Crop Insurance  
Corporation, U.S. Department of  
Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:  
Peter F. Cole, Secretary, Federal Crop  
Insurance Corporation, U.S. Department  
of Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250,  
telephone 202-447-3325.
The correction is as follows:
In the list of counties where sunflower  
crop insurance is otherwise authorized  
to be offered, as appearing on page  
75374 (44 FR 75374), the list under the  
subheading “North Dakota”, is hereby  
corrected by inserting alphabetically the  
following counties:
Bottineau, Mercer.
Issued in Washington, D.C., on February 6, 
1980.
Peter F. Cole,
Secretary, Federal Crop Insurance 
Corporation.
